The proposed approach is designated as Dynamic Prompt Specialization (DPS). DPS employs a small, high-speed auxiliary model—a semantic micro-model—that continuously analyzes the semantic and communicative structure of the current user input, extracts concise semantic fragments, and maps them to a predefined code table. Each code corresponds to a pre-engineered and validated prompt fragment, optionally accompanied by a confidence level or signal intensity score. Based on the active set of signals, DPS constructs a dynamic specialized context transmitted to the unmodified primary LLM. The primary goal of DPS is user interaction personalization: the system can adapt to stable individual communication patterns, ongoing conversational context, professional expertise level, task domain, feedback to previous answers, and other observable signals. Furthermore, DPS is not restricted to user communication. The same architecture can be applied to domain-specific pre-specialization of queries prior to reaching the primary LLM. This pre-structures multi-faceted queries and potentially reduces the necessity for dedicated specialist agents and complex orchestration pipelines. DPS operates without altering main model weights or requiring retraining. In the absence of a sufficiently confident signal, the system defaults to the baseline behavior of the main LLM. Consequently, DPS represents an orthogonal adaptation layer that can be integrated into existing LLM infrastructure without altering the underlying foundation model. 1. Problem Statement The proposed approach addresses two interconnected constraints in current LLM-based systems. 1.1. Scaling Does Not Solve Individual Specialization The main vector of foundation model advancement focuses on increasing: Parameter counts; Training data volume; Compute resources; Training duration and complexity; Model update frequency. However, expanding overall model capabilities does not yield a proportional enhancement in interaction quality for a specific individual user. In many practical scenarios, a user operates within a relatively bounded domain of knowledge and exhibits consistent individual patterns of task formulation, communication, verification, clarification, and correction. Thus, incremental general model knowledge often carries less practical utility than the system's ability to precisely align with a specific user's traits and the current interaction state. DPS shifts part of the specialization process from model parameter modification to dynamic context adaptation. 1.2. Static System Prompt Most LLM systems rely on a single primary system prompt or a narrow set of predefined instructions. As a result, interactions are typically treated as static: $$\text{System Instructions} \longrightarrow \text{User Request} \longrightarrow \text{Response}$$ DPS frames interaction as a dynamic process where conversational state evolves continuously: $$\text{Current User Signal} \longrightarrow \text{Analysis} \longrightarrow \text{Active Context Update} \longrightarrow \text{Response} \longrightarrow \text{New User Signal} \longrightarrow \text{State Update}$$ Thus, specialization occurs continuously rather than as a single static setup. 2. Core DPS Architecture DPS comprises three functionally separated layers, each holding distinct responsibilities. 2.1. Semantic Micro-Model – Fast Semantic Layer The first layer consists of a lightweight, ultra-fast auxiliary model. It is not designed for full reasoning or final output generation. Its scope is narrowly constrained to: Analyzing input utterances; Extracting short semantic fragments; Identifying corresponding semantic signals; Mapping signals to designated codes; Computing confidence or intensity levels for each signal. A typical semantic fragment may consist of a few words, though the architecture does not impose fixed-length constraints. Fragment size depends on input signal characteristics and implementation design. A single user turn can simultaneously trigger multiple independent codes. For instance, a query might concurrently express: Professional technical context; Financial domain context; Request for conciseness; Requirement for high precision; Emotional tone/signal; Affirmation of a previously established rule. Consequently, DPS is not forced to select a single category or agent, but instead builds a multidimensional set of co-active signals. 2.2. Code-Prompt Correspondence Table The second layer operates as a mapping repository: Code (e.g., PFA-0281) $\rightarrow$ Pre-engineered Prompt Fragment. A key principle of DPS is that prompt fragments are not automatically generated by the system on the fly. They are authored by engineers and undergo a controlled lifecycle: $$\text{Design} \longrightarrow \text{Testing} \longrightarrow \text{Verification} \longrightarrow \text{Approval} \longrightarrow \text{Deployment}$$ This establishes prompt engineering as a structured software engineering discipline. Codes map to behavioral, domain, or contextual specializations, such as: Technical engineering; Software programming; Financial analysis; Scientific discussion; Conversational interaction; Concise messaging; In-depth explanation; Critical evaluation; Re-affirmation of established context. 2.3. Dynamic Composite Prompt At the third layer, active codes are compiled into a unified composite context. Each signal maintains an intensity score, denoted internally as a temperature signal—a metric reflecting the activation strength of the given signal. Note: This term is distinct from the generation temperature parameter used in LLM sampling. DPS temperature measures signal activation strength rather than generative randomness. Based on these active signals, the system constructs a Composite Prompt passed to the primary LLM. Crucially, the primary LLM: Undergoes no retraining; Retains its original weights; Requires no specialized model variant; Executes a standard single generation pass. 3. Dynamic Temperature Profile – Breadcrumb State A core feature of DPS is that user profiling is not a one-off classification. It exists as a dynamic interaction state termed the Breadcrumb State. Profiling begins during the first exchanges of a conversation, eliminating the need to aggregate multiple historical sessions before initial activation. As dialogue progresses, individual signals can strengthen ($\uparrow$), weaken ($\downarrow$), disappear, be superseded, or interact with other active signals. Signal Dimension Trend Professional context $\uparrow$ Conciseness $\uparrow$ Need for detailed explanation $\downarrow$ Resistance to suggestion $\uparrow$ Confirmation of understanding $\uparrow$ This enables tracking not only topic content, but the evolving communicative dynamics of the session. 4. User Personalization The main purpose of DPS is adapting system behavior to an individual user. Across recurring sessions, a profile can persist (stored on the user side as a table of code mappings and signal temperatures) and evolve. Over time, the system continuously adapts to: Consistent professional contexts; Preferred task formulation styles; Desired response depth; Typical modes of confirmation or disagreement; Receptivity to suggestions; Preferred level of directness; Recurring communication patterns. This does not alter core LLM weights; instead, the interaction context shifts, allowing a single foundation model to serve diverse users through distinct dynamic adaptation profiles. 5. Professional Specialization Personalization does not degrade technical rigor. DPS can serve as a domain-specialization pre-layer between user requests and the primary LLM. When a user simultaneously addresses a technical problem, financial constraints, demands rigorous analysis, cites prior rules, and signals skepticism, traditional agentic architectures route the query through multiple stages: $$\text{Router} \longrightarrow \text{Technical Agent} \longrightarrow \text{Financial Agent} \longrightarrow \text{Context Aggregator} \longrightarrow \text{Main LLM}$$ DPS streamlines this pathway: $$\text{User Input} \longrightarrow \text{Semantic Micro-Model} \longrightarrow \text{Active Codes Selection} \longrightarrow \text{Composite Prompt} \longrightarrow \text{Main LLM}$$ Multiple context facets are integrated into a single pre-generation context, avoiding multi-agent pipeline overhead. 6. Reducing Agentic Complexity Modern AI implementations frequently rely on multi-agent orchestration: $$\text{Router} \longrightarrow \text{Specialist Agents (A, B, C)} \longrightarrow \text{Aggregator} \longrightarrow \text{Final LLM}$$ While effective, this paradigm increases inference latency, model call counts, compute costs, context size, and orchestration complexity. title: 基于量子态的概率模型构建
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of quantum state properties to construct a probabilistic model for quantum system evolution and states. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on classical probability distributions, but this work proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve a more precise description of quantum systems and potentially unlock significant advantages within the field of quantum computing. The core of this research lies in the design of a probabilistic model predicated on the unique characteristics of quantum states, offering a potential pathway toward enhanced accuracy and a fundamentally different perspective on quantum system dynamics. The paper presents the model's structure, underlying principles, and potential applications, emphasizing the significance of quantum states in shaping the probabilistic landscape of quantum systems.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks for Quantum Feature Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Self-Organizing Neural Networks (SONNs) to quantum feature learning, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and dynamic quantum state evolution. The core claim is that this approach enables the creation of more nuanced and deeper feature representations, ultimately improving model accuracy within the context of quantum computation. We explore how quantum-enhanced feature learning can be achieved through a novel dynamic adjustment process based on the interplay between quantum states and neural network weights. The study focuses on the potential of this methodology to address challenges associated with traditional feature extraction methods in quantum algorithms.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Neural Network Architectures via Genetic Programming
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neural network design utilizing genetic programming. The core idea is to leverage an evolutionary algorithm – a genetic algorithm – to dynamically adapt the architecture of a neural network. Traditional neural network design relies heavily on manual architecture specification and iterative weight tuning. This work shifts the focus to directly evolving the network's structure, offering a potentially more efficient and robust solution for complex tasks. The system iteratively modifies the network's architecture – adding or removing layers, adjusting connection parameters – based on the network's performance. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations associated with fixed architectures and manual design processes. The key innovation lies in the automated, iterative refinement of the network's structure, enabling it to self-adapt to varying input data and task requirements. This research contributes to the growing field of neuro-evolution, providing a framework for creating highly specialized and optimized neural networks without the constraints of predefined structures. The system evaluates performance using a defined fitness function, and the genetic algorithm guides the search for optimal architecture.

title: Dynamic Probability Field-Driven Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability field-driven optimization algorithm, leveraging the power of Gaussian processes to efficiently address complex optimization problems. The algorithm employs a dynamic probability field to transform the optimization problem into a series of controlled Gaussian processes, thereby accelerating the optimization process and enhancing overall efficiency. The core mechanism centers around utilizing Gaussian processes to manage the uncertainty inherent in the optimization landscape, providing a robust and adaptable approach to challenging problems. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through rigorous analysis and preliminary experimental validation across a range of optimization scenarios.

title: 基于图的几何证明的自动验证
abstract: This paper introduces a novel automatic verification method based on graph representation, aiming to enhance the reliability of geometric proofs. Traditional geometric proof verification relies heavily on manual inspection and validation, often requiring significant effort and potential for human error. We propose a system that transforms geometric proofs into graphical representations, facilitating automated verification through graph traversal and analysis. The core mechanism revolves around representing the geometric proof as a graph, enabling efficient validation through pathfinding and constraint satisfaction. This approach offers a significant improvement in verification speed and robustness, particularly for complex proofs. We detail the methodology, present preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness, and discuss future research directions, focusing on scalability and adaptability to diverse geometric proofs.

title: Geometric Information Theory for Quantum State Generation and Computation
abstract: Geometric Information Theory (GIT) offers a novel approach to quantum state generation and computation, leveraging geometric structures to encode and manipulate quantum states. This paper investigates the potential of GIT to enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. We explore the concept of utilizing geometric transformations and geometric information to optimize quantum state representations and control, ultimately aiming to improve the performance of quantum computation. The core claim is that by explicitly modeling quantum states through geometric structures, we can achieve a significant improvement in efficiency and scalability. This work presents a framework for applying GIT principles to specific quantum algorithms, focusing on key areas such as state manipulation, quantum error correction, and optimization of quantum circuits. The paper will delve into the mathematical foundations of GIT, demonstrate the practical implementation of key algorithms, and analyze the potential benefits of this approach. We will also discuss the challenges and future directions for this burgeoning field.

title: ##基于神经符号人工智能的知识推理系统
abstract: This paper proposes a novel knowledge reasoning system based on neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence. The core idea is to integrate the strengths of neural computation and symbolic reasoning to achieve robust and interpretable knowledge inference. We leverage neural networks to learn efficient and flexible knowledge representations from data, while employing symbolic reasoning techniques to perform logical deduction and inference on these representations. The system architecture consists of a neural knowledge encoder, a symbolic inference engine, and a feedback loop for refining both components. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline key challenges and future research directions. The system aims to bridge the gap between the statistical learning capabilities of neural networks and the logical rigor of symbolic AI, leading to a more powerful and explainable AI. ---

title: Adaptive Quantum State Interference
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum state interference algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional quantum information processing methods. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the interference matrix based on the system state, enabling more precise quantum information handling. We present a novel approach that leverages a feedback mechanism to optimize the interference pattern for specific quantum states. The core mechanism focuses on iterative refinement of the interference matrix, ensuring optimal performance across a range of input conditions. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved accuracy and robustness compared to static interference schemes, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic system changes. This advancement holds significant implications for the design and implementation of advanced quantum algorithms.

title: Adaptive State Measure of Quantum States
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit remarkable complexity, and efficient parameter optimization is crucial for achieving desired outcomes. This paper introduces a novel adaptive state measure, designed to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters based on the system's inherent dynamics. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, rendering them inadequate for highly dynamic systems. Our approach leverages the inherent information contained within quantum states to automatically optimize system behavior. This adaptive measure promises to significantly enhance quantum system performance through a proactive and automated parameter tuning process. The core mechanism centers around quantifying and responding to the system's state evolution through a carefully constructed, self-adjusting metric.

title: Decentralized Differential Privacy via Federated Learning with Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: This paper presents a novel decentralized differential privacy protocol for federated learning, integrating homomorphic encryption and differential privacy to achieve enhanced data protection. The proposed system addresses the challenges of privacy preservation and scalability inherent in traditional federated learning approaches. Users locally compute on their datasets, encrypting the results before transmitting them to a central aggregator. The aggregator performs computations on these encrypted datasets, adding noise to ensure differential privacy. The core innovation lies in the synergistic combination of homomorphic encryption for secure computation and differential privacy for privacy guarantees, resulting in a robust and scalable decentralized solution. The system's architecture minimizes data exposure and strengthens privacy protection while facilitating collaborative learning across multiple devices. This approach provides a viable pathway for privacy-sensitive applications leveraging the collective intelligence of distributed data.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Representation Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to representation learning utilizing adaptive kernel learning. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the kernel function within kernel methods, responding to the evolving characteristics of the data. Instead of relying on predefined kernels, we employ a recurrent neural network (RNN) to learn the kernel's parameters directly from the data. This allows the representation learning process to adapt to non-stationary data distributions, a significant challenge in many real-world scenarios. The proposed method offers a more flexible and potentially more effective representation learning tool compared to traditional kernel methods that utilize fixed kernels. We detail the architecture, training procedure, and theoretical underpinnings of this adaptive kernel learning framework, highlighting its potential advantages and future research directions. The key mathematical formulation revolves around the kernel function, denoted as *K*(s1, s2, ..., sK), and the RNN's parameter update, expressed as ∂*K*/∂θ = η∇L, where θ represents the parameters of the kernel function, η is the learning rate, and L is the loss function. The RNN is trained to minimize the loss, which is typically a measure of the discrepancy between the learned representations and a desired target. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual illustrations, paving the way for further development and experimentation.

title: 拓扑信息融合的动态概率模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability model based on topology information fusion. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with complex environments due to their static nature. Topology information fusion aims to improve prediction and control accuracy by dynamically adjusting probability distributions based on the structural relationships within the system. We propose a framework that integrates multiple probability distributions through a dynamic weighting mechanism, effectively capturing intricate dependencies and enhancing model robustness. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a "topology-aware" probability distribution, allowing the model to adapt to changing conditions and improve generalization performance. This research offers a new approach to probabilistic modeling, addressing limitations of existing methods and potentially leading to significant advancements in various applications requiring accurate predictions and control.

title: Bicolor-Spined Porcupine: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Unique Morphology of the Porcupine
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Bicolor-Spined Porcupine (BCSP), inspired by the distinctive morphology of the bicolor-spined porcupine (Erethizon dorsatum). The algorithm leverages the porcupine's unique defense mechanism – the strategic placement of spines – to effectively navigate complex optimization problems. BCSP utilizes a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a 'spine' representation and a 'spiking' mechanism to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the 'spine density' and 'spike intensity' based on the algorithm's convergence behavior. We demonstrate BCSP's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional metaheuristic methods in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's parameterization, particularly the 'spine density' and 'spike intensity' parameters, are discussed in detail. Future research directions include integrating BCSP with other optimization techniques and exploring its application in real-world engineering problems.

title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning Dynamic Reward Structure
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive reinforcement learning framework designed to dynamically adjust reward structures within an environment. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on static reward functions, limiting the framework's adaptability. We propose a system that leverages self-adaptive learning to construct and refine reward functions on the fly, optimizing for both immediate reward and long-term performance. The core mechanism involves a continuous, iterative process of environment modeling, reward function adaptation, and learning. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods by addressing the inherent challenges of adapting to dynamic environments. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of this framework in a simulated environment, illustrating its ability to achieve superior performance compared to baseline methods.

title: Beringian Brown Lemming: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Cyclic Dynamics of a Lemming Population
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Beringian Brown Lemming" (BBL), inspired by the population dynamics of the Beringian brown lemming. Lemmings exhibit a characteristic cyclic population boom and bust, driven by complex interactions between predator-prey relationships, resource availability, and environmental factors. BBL leverages this cyclical behavior to generate a new optimization strategy. The algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and employs a 'nesting' mechanism analogous to lemming burrows for solution preservation and exploration. The core of BBL involves a cyclic update strategy influenced by lemming population size, combined with a local search component mimicking predator-prey dynamics. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. Key aspects of the algorithm include a dynamic parameter control based on population size fluctuations and a novel convergence criterion based on the variance of solution populations. The results indicate that BBL provides a competitive solution approach for diverse optimization challenges, exhibiting robustness and efficiency.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Benguela Dolphin Algorithm" (BDA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Benguela dolphins. These dolphins exhibit sophisticated strategies for locating prey in dynamic and uncertain environments. BDA leverages these strategies—specifically, their echolocation, cooperative search, and adaptive movement patterns—to create an effective optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates key elements such as a "sonar pulse" for exploration, a "cooperative search" mechanism simulating dolphin groups, and an "adaptive movement" strategy based on environmental feedback. Mathematical formulations for the core components, including the position update equation, the probability of movement, and the fitness evaluation function are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its potential for tackling complex and challenging tasks. The algorithm is designed to be robust, adaptable, and computationally efficient, offering a viable alternative to existing metaheuristic methods. The key performance metrics, like convergence rate and solution quality, are analyzed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the BDA. The goal is to provide a novel and efficient optimization method inspired by nature.

title: ##基于量子神经网络的特征提取与分类
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) for advanced feature extraction and classification tasks. Classical neural networks often struggle with complex datasets and computational bottlenecks. QNNs, leveraging principles of quantum mechanics like entanglement and superposition, offer a fundamentally different approach. This research investigates the construction and application of a QNN architecture designed to exploit these quantum properties. We present a model utilizing quantum gates and qubits to perform parallel computations and generate more effective feature representations compared to traditional neural networks. The core claim of this work is the demonstration of QNNs surpassing the performance of classical networks in complex classification problems. We detail the theoretical framework, model design, and discuss the potential impact of QNNs on various applications, highlighting their ability to unlock new levels of accuracy and efficiency in data analysis. The key mechanisms driving this potential are the inherent parallelism and superior feature representation capabilities of QNNs.

title: Bayesian Resonance Networks for Temporal Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Resonance Networks (BRNs) – a novel neural network architecture designed to model and predict temporal dynamics with superior accuracy compared to existing recurrent and long short-term memory (LSTM) models. We propose a Bayesian framework to dynamically weight data points based on historical resonance frequencies, fostering long-term predictive capabilities. The BRN's core mechanism leverages the inherent time-dependent nature of complex systems, offering a fundamentally different approach to temporal forecasting. This research provides a rigorous theoretical foundation and practical implementation demonstrating the potential of BRNs to excel in predicting complex temporal patterns across diverse domains.

title: ## The Octopod Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Octopus Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Octopod Algorithm (OA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique hunting strategies of octopuses. Octopuses employ a decentralized, adaptive approach to prey capture, utilizing tentacle movements and camouflage to maximize their chances of success. The OA mimics these behaviors by employing a population of 'tentacles' representing potential solutions, each independently exploring the search space. Tentacle movement is governed by a stochastic process influenced by both local gradient information and global population consensus, mirroring the octopus's simultaneous pursuit and adaptation. The algorithm incorporates a 'camouflage' mechanism, dynamically adjusting solution weights based on their fitness relative to the population average, further enhancing exploration and exploitation. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, mathematical formulations, and a conceptual overview of its implementation, highlighting its potential advantages in complex optimization problems.

title: Title: Dynamic Graph Embedding for Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: Dynamic graph embedding is a novel approach to representing graphs, allowing the embedding to adapt to the learning algorithm's performance, thereby enhancing the model's robustness and efficiency. This paper introduces a dynamic graph embedding technique that dynamically adjusts the representation of a graph based on observed performance metrics. We propose a method that iteratively updates the embedding vector, ensuring a constant level of representation while adapting to the specific characteristics of the graph being processed. The core mechanism is based on a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the performance of the learning algorithm and adjusts the embedding vector accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through experiments on various graph datasets, showcasing improvements in model performance and generalization. Keywords: Graph Embedding, Dynamic Graph Embedding, Adaptive Machine Learning, Feedback Loop, Representation Learning.

title: ## Ashy-bellied Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Ashy-bellied Oldfield Mouse (AOM), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the ash-bellied oldfield mouse (Mineteus furfuraceus). This algorithm leverages the mouse's adaptive search strategy, focusing on efficient resource exploration and exploitation, to solve complex optimization problems. AOM employs a unique population management scheme based on 'patch hopping' and 'resource prioritization' mimicking the mouse's movement patterns and food selection. The algorithm incorporates a novel convergence criterion based on the variance of resource utilization, aiming to accelerate convergence while maintaining exploration capabilities. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's properties and its potential for competitive performance across various benchmark optimization problems. Simulation results on benchmark functions like Rastrigin, Sphere, and Ackley demonstrate that AOM can achieve comparable or superior results to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in a reasonable computational time. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Foraging Behavior, Patch Hopping, Resource Prioritization, Convergence Criterion, Adaptive Population Management. ---

title: Adaptive Distributed Data Compression with Quantum Annealing
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to distributed data compression leveraging the capabilities of quantum annealing. The core challenge in distributed data compression lies in striking a balance between achieving high compression ratios and minimizing communication overhead across a network. Traditional methods often rely on heuristic algorithms, which can be inefficient and fail to adapt to varying network conditions and data dependencies. We propose a framework where quantum annealing is employed to solve the complex optimization problem of determining the optimal compression strategy for a distributed data stream. The framework incorporates key factors such as network bandwidth limitations, data redundancy, and potential correlations between data elements. The objective function within the quantum annealing algorithm is designed to maximize compression efficiency while adhering to communication constraints. Preliminary simulations demonstrate the potential of this approach to surpass the performance of conventional methods in dynamic and heterogeneous distributed environments. The research contributes to a more adaptive and intelligent approach to data compression, opening possibilities for improved bandwidth utilization and reduced storage requirements in distributed systems.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric error correction within complex simulations. title: Dynamic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Large State Spaces – Hierarchical Abstraction
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, yet its application is often hindered by the computational complexity associated with large state spaces. Traditional dynamic programming algorithms, such as Value Iteration and Policy Iteration, suffer severely from the curse of dimensionality, rendering them impractical for problems with a vast number of states. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by integrating hierarchical dynamic programming with learned abstraction layers. We decompose the state space into a hierarchy of abstraction levels, employing autoencoders to learn low-dimensional representations (embeddings) at each level. These embeddings facilitate efficient state aggregation and enable the application of dynamic programming within the hierarchical structure. The core idea is to reduce the problem size by representing the state space with a hierarchy of compact, learned representations, thereby mitigating the computational burden. This approach offers a scalable solution for RL problems with large state spaces, presenting a significant advancement in the field.

title: Quantum-Inspired Hardware Acceleration for Deep Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to hardware acceleration for deep learning by leveraging principles inspired by quantum mechanics. Traditional hardware acceleration methods for deep learning are largely based on classical architectures and operations. This research proposes designing hardware accelerators that mimic key quantum phenomena, namely superposition and entanglement, to enhance the efficiency of core deep learning operations. The architecture utilizes probabilistic computing and carefully constructed hardware elements to approximate quantum algorithms, offering a fundamentally different paradigm for accelerating deep learning workloads. The presented framework provides a theoretical foundation and a design methodology for creating quantum-inspired hardware, potentially overcoming the limitations of conventional approaches. This work highlights a promising direction for future deep learning hardware development.

title: # Andean Bear: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Andean Bear Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Bear Algorithm (ABA), designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of the Andean bear, a solitary and highly adaptable animal known for its efficient resource utilization and strategic decision-making in challenging environments. ABA leverages concepts of exploration, exploitation, and memory of good solutions, mimicking the Andean bear's ability to balance searching for new food sources with consolidating existing ones. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive mutation operator based on the bear's scent marking behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABA through simulations across several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitiveness against established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics including convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness. The results suggest that ABA is a promising approach for tackling a broad range of optimization challenges.

title: A Cognitive Neuroscience-Inspired Programming Language Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to programming language design, drawing inspiration from the principles of cognitive neuroscience. The core claim is that by incorporating concepts such as attention mechanisms and memory encoding, we can significantly enhance the efficiency and understandability of programming. Traditional programming languages often lack a direct connection to human cognitive processes, resulting in reduced developer productivity and increased complexity. This design introduces a language that mimics cognitive functions, offering a more intuitive and effective development experience. Specifically, the language incorporates an "attention mechanism" that automatically highlights and prioritizes critical code segments. This approach aims to bridge the gap between computer science and cognitive science, leading to a more natural and productive programming paradigm. The paper details the core design principles, including the syntax and semantics informed by cognitive neuroscience, and outlines the potential benefits of this new programming language.

title: Meta-Learning for Automated Algorithm Selection in Scientific Simulations
abstract: The selection of an appropriate algorithm is a critical, yet frequently manual and iterative, step in scientific simulation. This paper proposes a meta-learning framework designed to automate this process. The system learns from a diverse set of simulation tasks, extracting features related to the simulation's domain, complexity, and desired accuracy requirements. Based on this learned knowledge, the system then predicts and selects the algorithm most likely to yield optimal results for a *new*, unseen simulation. The core of the approach lies in leveraging meta-learning techniques to efficiently acquire and generalize algorithmic selection strategies. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining a potential architecture and key considerations for implementation, highlighting the potential for significant time savings and accelerated scientific discovery. The proposed method addresses the inherent challenge of algorithm selection by transforming it from a human-driven, often suboptimal, process into a learned, predictive system.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Differential Privacy for Scientific Data
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to collaborative scientific data analysis leveraging Decentralized Federated Learning with Differential Privacy (DFLDP). The core challenge in many scientific domains is the reluctance to share raw data due to stringent privacy regulations and intellectual property protections. Traditional Federated Learning (FL) solutions, while offering a degree of data privacy, still rely on centralized aggregation, a point of vulnerability. Our proposed DFLDP framework addresses this limitation by adopting a decentralized architecture where individual researchers maintain complete control over their datasets. Crucially, we integrate differential privacy mechanisms directly into the aggregation process, adding a quantifiable layer of protection against data leakage. This ensures that the learned model benefits from the collective knowledge of multiple researchers without revealing individual data contributions. The system utilizes a gossip-based communication protocol for model updates, minimizing communication overhead. We formally define the mathematical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system's performance is evaluated in a simulated environment, demonstrating the effectiveness of the DFLDP approach in achieving accurate models while upholding stringent privacy guarantees. The core claim of this work is that sharing raw scientific data for federated learning is often prohibited due to privacy concerns and intellectual property restrictions. The core mechanism implemented is the realization of a federated learning system that utilizes differential privacy to protect data during aggregation, while also employing a decentralized architecture where individual researchers retain control over their data. This new approach combines federated learning with differential privacy and decentralization, enabling collaborative scientific discovery without compromising data privacy or intellectual property rights.

ACM leverages these principles to develop a robust and efficient optimization strategy. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cauchy-Matthewmann Mutation (CMM) with a novel altitude-inspired adjustment mechanism. Specifically, the algorithm dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation parameters based on a simulated "altitude pressure" – a measure of the search space's complexity. ACM's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitiveness against established metaheuristic methods. The key innovations of ACM lie in its adaptive parameter control and the incorporation of a concept analogous to acclimatization observed in chinchillas, enabling it to effectively navigate challenging optimization landscapes. The algorithm's complexity is analyzed, and its strengths and limitations are discussed.

title: On Information Bottleneck Theory-Based Neural Connection Weight Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network learning algorithm grounded in the principles of the Information Bottleneck (IB) theory. The algorithm aims to effectively learn the relationships and dependencies between neurons by strategically manipulating connection weights. The core mechanism relies on the IB theory's constraint that the representation of a variable should capture only the relevant information about that variable while discarding irrelevant details. Specifically, the learning process strives to induce a bottleneck state in the information flow between neurons, forcing them to focus on the most salient features. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and robust learning method compared to traditional weight adjustment techniques, particularly in scenarios where the underlying data is high-dimensional and contains significant noise. The algorithm is described in detail, outlining the key parameters, the learning objective, and the mathematical formulation of the weight update rule. Simulation results (described in the subsequent sections) demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy in capturing relevant dependencies and achieving competitive performance.

title: Dynamic Semantic Embedding Network (DSE-Net)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Embedding Network (DSE-Net), a novel approach to understanding evolving data streams. The core claim is that by integrating semantic embeddings with dynamic graph neural networks, we can achieve continuous, context-aware understanding, overcoming the limitations of static embedding models. DSE-Net employs a multi-layered architecture: a Transformer encoder for initial semantic embedding generation, a dynamic graph neural network (GNN) to model relationships within the data stream, and a reinforcement learning (RL) module to optimize the GNN's structure and parameters adaptively. Crucially, the embedding itself is updated based on the GNN's output, creating an evolving semantic representation. This approach addresses the shortcomings of existing methods, which either rely on static embeddings or static GNNs, by providing a dynamic and learning system capable of adapting to changing semantic relationships. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of these techniques, leading to a more robust and nuanced understanding of dynamic data. ---

title: White Heron Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WHM-OA)
abstract: This paper introduces the White Heron Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WHM-OA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of white herons. Unlike traditional metaheuristic algorithms, WHM-OA incorporates a dynamic weighting mechanism based on the heron's observation of the search space, mimicking their strategic movement towards promising regions. The algorithm utilizes a population of agents, each representing a potential solution. Each agent's movement is governed by a combination of random exploration and exploitation, modulated by a heuristic function that dynamically adjusts the influence of past successful movements. The core innovation lies in the 'Heron's Glance' mechanism, where agents periodically assess the overall landscape and adjust their individual movement probabilities based on the relative density of promising solutions. This paper details the algorithm's formulation, including the key parameters and their impact on performance, and provides a theoretical foundation for its effectiveness. The algorithm's design aims to provide a robust and efficient approach to solving complex optimization problems.

title: Alexander's Cusimanse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Cusimanse
abstract: This paper presents Alexander's Cusimanse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the behavior of the cusimanse ( *Cusimanche* ), a small, highly agile rodent native to the Iberian Peninsula. The cusimanse's rapid, erratic movements, particularly its ability to navigate complex environments with remarkable efficiency, serve as the core inspiration for the algorithm's design. Alexander's Cusimanse employs a hybrid approach, combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) to achieve robust exploration and exploitation capabilities. The algorithm utilizes a novel "Adaptive Velocity" mechanism, mimicking the cusimanse's quick directional changes, and a "Terrain-Aware" update rule, reflecting its efficient pathfinding strategy. Theoretical analysis suggests that the algorithm's design promotes a balance between premature convergence and effective exploration. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness across a range of benchmark problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The key contributions of this work are the introduction of the Adaptive Velocity mechanism and the Terrain-Aware update rule, providing a novel approach to metaheuristic optimization inspired by a fascinating animal behavior.

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑张图的计算
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement for accelerating the computation of topological maps. Traditional approaches to topological map computation are computationally intensive, often requiring significant time and resources. We propose a novel method leveraging quantum entanglement to provide a more efficient and potentially scalable solution. This involves the creation and manipulation of entangled states to effectively explore the topological structure of the map, ultimately leading to a simplified computation. The core mechanism relies on exploiting the inherent correlations in entangled systems to reduce the complexity of the problem. This paper presents the theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. We highlight the advantages of quantum entanglement in enhancing computational speed and exploring novel topological map representations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for research in this area.

abstract: Quantum algorithms are increasingly crucial for tackling complex quantum systems, demanding novel approaches to their design and optimization. Traditional algorithmic design often neglects the inherent topological structure of quantum systems, limiting our ability to effectively leverage these structures for improved performance. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm based on topological structures, offering a fundamentally new perspective on algorithm design. We propose a method for dynamically generating and manipulating quantum parameters through the incorporation of topological constraints, thereby optimizing the algorithm's performance for specific quantum systems exhibiting complex topologies. The core mechanism involves utilizing topological concepts to define the algorithm's parameters and guide its execution, resulting in enhanced efficiency and adaptability. This research addresses a critical gap in quantum algorithm development, providing a framework for tackling problems with intricate topological properties.

title: Core Claim: Designing a quantum topology cipher system based on quantum entanglement, its security relies on the fragility of quantum topology, and provides enhanced resilience against attacks.
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly emerging field, offers a fundamentally new approach to cryptography by exploiting the inherent fragility of topological structures. We present a novel cryptographic protocol centered around the exploitation of quantum entanglement, utilizing the unique properties of topological spaces to ensure enhanced resilience against various attacks. The core mechanism involves constructing a key distribution and decryption protocol that leverages the sensitivity of topological landscapes to maintain security. This work aims to establish a quantum-enhanced cipher that surpasses current cryptographic methods through a fundamentally different approach to security. The study will focus on the mathematical underpinnings of topological cryptography and demonstrate the practical application of this approach, particularly through a detailed analysis of the protocol's security properties and resilience against known attacks. title: CAKE : Energy-aware crypto-agile key management for energy-harvesting IoT with runtime switching between ASCON-128 and ML-KEM
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are expected to operate in environments where the available power is dynamic and uncertain.This leads to a stark security vs. energy consumption trade-off in post-quantum cryptography.While modern post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) primitives like ML-KEM (Kyber-512) provide strong quantum-secure security, they are computationally expensive and require large amounts of energy.In this paper, an energy-aware key management protocol Crypto-Agile Key Exchange, CAKE is proposed.CAKE is evaluated using a simulation framework targeted to a Cortex-M4 based IoT node that operates under realistics solar energy harvesting settings.Our results demonstrate that proposed protocol achieves zero session drops at the node for up to 10,000 state transitions and it achieves a reduction of 47.3% in number of Kyber KEM operations in indoor settings, while it achieves an average transition time of 14.7 ms.Under constrained conditions, the proposed protocol is proven to be IND-CCA2 secure in the high-energy state, and 128-bit classical security is preserved in the low-energy state.

title: Semantic Web-based Knowledge Graph Construction of Chemical Accident Data and Latent Risk Identification through Ontology Reasoning
abstract: Chemical accident data are collected separately by different countries and agencies, and their schemas, terms, and code systems do not match, which limits any single database for finding latent risks. To address this, we apply Semantic Web technology to the chemical safety domain, integrating heterogeneous chemical accident data into one knowledge graph and running ontology reasoning on top of it. From five sources covering the United States, the European Union, Germany, Japan, and South Korea, we gathered accident records and built an ontology that defines substances, processes, equipment, causes, and consequences as classes, then linked to form the knowledge graph. Reasoning based on the class hierarchy and rules worked as intended, and by crossing the class axes of hazard properties, processes, and equipment, we identified latent risk combinations that were not stated in any single record. Maintenance work on tanks holding flammable substances showed a serious accident rate about ten times the overall baseline, and a statistical test confirmed that this risk becomes significant only when the three factors occur together. This study shows that ontology based knowledge structuring can support both the integration of heterogeneous data and the discovery of latent risks. As future work, we suggest formalizing these findings as rules and extending them to dynamic risk assessment linked with Korea's three major chemical laws and external chemical safety systems.

title: Improving Scholarly Knowledge Organization with Neuro-Symbolic and Human-in-the-Loop Approaches
abstract: Scholarly knowledge remains locked within unstructured documents, limiting machine processing, reuse, and cross-paper synthesis. This dissertation investigates how hybrid neuro-symbolic and human-in-the-loop methods can enable scalable, high-quality structuring of scholarly knowledge within the Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG). We argue that effective scholarly knowledge organization requires a progression from human-guided symbolic foundations to hybrid neuro-symbolic methods, with human-in-the-loop validation integrated throughout. This dissertation makes five contributions organized in two phases. The first phase establishes symbolic foundations. The Knowledge Graph Maturity Model (KGMM), a multi-level maturity model for scholarly knowledge graph quality, provides a structured framework for assessing and guiding knowledge graph development across seven quality dimensions. A reproducibility score based on four pillars derived from the FAIR principles enables automated assessment of research artifact interlinking. An empirical assessment of 92 ORKG contributions yielded a mean score of 93.0%. The second phase introduces neuro-symbolic augmentation that builds on these foundations. The Comparison Wizard combines large language models with knowledge graph structures and human validation for extracting structured comparisons from scientific papers. In a formative user study with 21 participants, 76.2% agreed on its value for automation and transparency. The ORKG Extension (ORKGEx) integrates language and vision-language models for multimodal annotation of research contributions across text and figures. In a formative evaluation with 11 participants, 9 of 11 (82%) reported positive overall satisfaction. Section-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (SARAG) leverages the inherent structure of scientific papers. In an expert evaluation involving 17 domain experts across 15 papers, SARAG attained an overall accuracy of 74.3% and a quality score of 80.4%, assessed through a novel three-way evaluation framework combining ground truth, automated metrics, and expertise-weighted human judgment. Across all user studies, given the sample sizes, the results are interpreted as indicative evidence of feasibility and perceived utility rather than statistically generalizable claims. Across all contributions, human expertise is strategically positioned within automated workflows rather than replaced by them. The results indicate that neither purely symbolic nor purely neural approaches suffice in isolation; their strategic integration, guided by human judgment, enables scalable scholarly knowledge organization that maintains the quality standards required for reliable real-world use.

title: Context Inference Attacks Without Jailbreaks
abstract: Agentic AI systems are increasingly deployed to process sensitive data at inference time, such as healthcare records or financial documents assembled into a hidden \emph{context} before the system answers. Prior work has studied privacy risks primarily through \emph{jailbreaking} attacks that induce models to directly disclose sensitive content, but has largely overlooked the agentic setting where the context is assembled by the agent's own tool calls. We show that the agents we evaluate remain vulnerable to hidden-context leakage despite the controls we test against them, namely an instruction not to disclose the context, logit suppression, and context dilution. For instance, a web-browsing agent answering benign user queries still carries exploitable signals about records silently loaded into its context. We introduce and formalize \emph{context-inference attacks} through a security game and evaluate three settings under decreasing attacker knowledge and increasingly indirect delivery of the context: a known context, an unknown context, and a context the agent retrieves through its own tool calls. We distinguish a grey-box setting, in which the target model is used to score observations, from black-box settings in which the attacker scores with a surrogate it controls. We further characterize how leakage varies with query budget, context size, and target-model size. A single attack carries through all three settings without modification, reaching $100\%$ ASR on small candidate sets and $63\%$ at $1024$ candidates against a known context, $78.9$ AUROC when the template and surrounding records are unknown, $92.5$ AUROC when a 14B surrogate scores a 32B target, and $81.8$ AUROC when the records arrive as an agent's retrieval returns, against chance rates of $1/|\mathcal{Z}|$ and $50$ respectively.

title: Reading the News: Adapting Large Language Models to Swedish Journalism Through Continued Pre-Training
abstract: Large language models are increasingly capable in general, but their utility can remain modest in niche or understudied areas. One approach to address this limitation is to specialise existing models through additional training on target-domain corpora. In this work, we investigate such continued pre-training for adapting large language models to Swedish journalism, using a high-quality dataset that we curate from millions of news articles. To evaluate the adaptation efficacy, we also construct a novel domain-specific benchmark that covers six editorial tasks. Through full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning across two model sizes, we find that continued pre-training yields benefits in the target domain, but only when paired with experience replay to mitigate forgetting. We observe consistent enhancements in the models' generation quality and factual knowledge, but not their proficiency in discriminative tasks. Exploring a training-free method to facilitate instruction following, we see further improvements, but exclusively for models trained with low-rank adaptation. Crucially, we demonstrate the importance of targeted evaluation in the adaptation process, as an existing Swedish benchmark largely fails to capture the models' in-domain performance gains.

Through full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning across two model sizes, we find that continued pre-training yields benefits in the target domain, but only when paired with experience replay to mitigate forgetting. We observe consistent enhancements in the models' generation quality and factual knowledge, but not their proficiency in discriminative tasks. Exploring a training-free method to facilitate instruction following, we see further improvements, but exclusively for models trained with low-rank adaptation. Crucially, we demonstrate the importance of targeted evaluation in the adaptation process, as an existing Swedish benchmark largely fails to capture the models' in-domain performance gains.

title: Lies We Can See: Joint Verbal and Non-Verbal Deception by VLM Agents in Embodied Social Interactions
abstract: Strategic deception by LLM and VLM agents has emerged as a central AI alignment and safety concern. Social-deduction games (where each player holds a hidden role and communicates with others to deduce identities) serve as the canonical testbed, particularly in multi-agent settings. Existing testbeds, however, are text-only and run on a single fixed agent configuration, missing the non-verbal sensorimotor channels treated as core by deception taxonomies and leaving it ambiguous whether an observed behavior reflects the underlying model or the surrounding harness. We introduce MineAmongUs, a 3D multimodal Among Us sandbox where imposter agents must deceive crewmates through joint verbal and non-verbal action. We also propose ARIA, a configurable VLM-agent harness that exposes five cognitive-component ablation axes; and an atom- and arc-level annotation scheme grounded in deception taxonomies and operationalized at scale by an LLM-as-a-Judge reaching near-human atom-labeling agreement. Empirical results show that VLM agents pursue imposter wins through joint verbal and non-verbal deception, with non-verbal channels emerging as the more decisive winning contributors across both harness ablation and cross-VLM evaluation. Taken together, our work opens a new path for embodied VLM-agent alignment research.

title: Generating Workflow DAGs from Natural Language with Non-Reasoning LLMs
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of translating natural-language routing rules written by business administrators into executable workflow graphs for enterprise contact centers. Each target is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of conditional actions with parallel branches, hit-first fallback chains, and per-branch Boolean predicates, encoded in the JSON dialect of a commercial routing platform. We show that neuro-symbolic decomposition enables lower-cost, non-reasoning large language models to generate complex workflow DAGs at production-relevant quality without expensive extended-reasoning models. Our central diagnostic is an emission-density bottleneck: on a 635-rule benchmark of manufactured synthetic data, models select the correct graph nodes with high accuracy but increasingly misconfigure attributes and Boolean grouping as the number of interdependent nodes emitted in one pass grows. We therefore move combinatorial graph construction from the model into a deterministic compiler driven by a compact intermediate representation, with a learned registry-selection front end that focuses generation on relevant vocabulary. Across four models, the full system reaches approximately 89% LLM-judge validity, approximately 90% exact-match condition accuracy, and 99-100% valid JSON while using roughly half the per-rule prompt tokens of a monolithic prompt. On GPT-5.3-chat, the method improves judge validity by 24 percentage points and achieves statistical equivalence to a reasoning model's out-of-the-box quality, although an approximately 8-point frontier gap remains. We also present a deployment path and transferable lessons for structured-generation applications.

title: Detecting Hidden Chain-of-Thought in Large Language Models with Linguistic, Behavioral, and Mechanistic Indicators
abstract: Large language models often answer complex reasoning questions without revealing intermediate steps, raising whether they reason latently or complete patterns. We propose the Hidden CoT Detection Score (HCDS), a comparative behavioral and mechanistic signal measuring whether neutral-prompt behavior aligns more closely with explicit CoT or explicit no- CoT. Here, hidden CoT operationally denotes this neutral-prompt CoT-like alignment; HCDS does not directly observe or prove an unexposed reasoning trace. On GSM8K, HCDS is significantly positive for both Qwen3-4B variants (Thinking $+1.87$, $p = 1.2 \times 10^{-7}$; Instruct $+1.41$, $p = 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$), replicates across a different inference stack and quantization within $0.08$ ($+1.80$ and $+1.45$), and is not significantly positive in seven of eight length-adjusted calibration-control cells. The unadjusted score produces large positive scores on single-step arithmetic and numeric factual lookup. The variants also respond differently to no-CoT instructions: Instruct complies from the prompt alone, whereas Thinking continues reasoning and requires intervention. These findings show stronger, less prompt-conditional CoT-like behavior in the reasoning-tuned model, consistent with but not proof of latent reasoning. HCDS thus investigates latent reasoning without relying on models' self-reported traces.

title: EMERGE-Policy: A Robot Mind Emerges Beyond a Single Policy
abstract: A robot's effective ``mind'' need not reside in a single policy. It can emerge when specialized components perceive, reason, predict, act, verify, and remember within a shared orchestration process. EMERGE-Policy turns this perspective into a graph-structured agentic framework that coordinates both capability invocation and information exchange. A Main Agent retains task-level state within an active context window, while role-specific Sub Agents process perception, execution monitoring, verification, and memory consolidation in isolated contexts and return structured, task-relevant evidence. Role-specific contexts control information load by exposing only decision-relevant evidence to the Main Agent, while the functional Skill interface composes heterogeneous backends as Operational, Imagination, and Evaluation Skills. Criterion-grounded verification, textual failure diagnosis, and Branch Stack recovery provide localized correction, with token-aware external memory preserving task-relevant state. Together, their closed-loop interaction realizes the system-level policy captured by the name EMERGE-Policy. Without additional fine-tuning, we achieved outstanding performance on several public benchmark that have had a wide-reaching impact, and conducted a series of real robot experiments. These system-level results suggest that through the division of different functional sub-tasks among multiple agents and their concurrent collaboration, as well as the technical paradigm where the model is regarded as a skill and called within the framework, EMERGE-Policy can extend the robust robot policies beyond isolated runs.

title: Harness-RL: Black-Box Reinforcement Learning with Action-Args Decoupling for Central-Agent Multi-Agent Harnesses
abstract: Large language model agents increasingly solve long-horizon tasks through multi-agent harnesses in which a central agent coordinates specialized sub-agents, tools, and environments. Training the central policy in such a harness raises two challenges. First, an action label is a low-cardinality decision, whereas its args form a high-dimensional conditional sequence; optimizing both with a shared sequence-level signal can produce conflicting gradients. Second, dynamic scheduling creates interdependent sessions with branches, parallel calls, and rewritten contexts, which cannot be faithfully reduced to one flat token sequence. We introduce Harness-RL, a structured reinforcement learning framework that combines Conflict-Aware Policy Optimization (CAPO) with interface-level black-box trajectory construction. The black-box component captures Interface Call Records, builds per-session prefix trees, and aligns outcome and process rewards with trainable tokens. CAPO uses forward activations to identify parameter partitions associated with action and args tokens, then routes their policy gradients to the corresponding subspaces. Harness-RL supports both central-only and joint multi-agent training. Across seven multi-hop question answering and agentic retrieval benchmarks, it reaches average F1 scores of 42.93 and 47.79 with Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-3B, respectively, while ablations validate the contribution of CAPO and favor central-only optimization in the evaluated setting. Our code is available at https://github.com/jiangxinke/Harness-RL.

title: GenRubric: Self-Evolving Rubric Generation for Scalable LLM Evaluation
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as scalable evaluators for open-ended tasks. However, many LLM judges derive query-specific criteria during scoring, leaving the evaluation requirements insufficiently specified and their coverage difficult to audit. Query-specific rubrics make these requirements explicit, but expert-written rubrics are costly to construct, while existing automatic methods typically rely on inference-time refinement or external supervision. We introduce GenRubric, a self-evolving framework that improves rubric generation from unlabeled queries without requiring additional human annotations during self-evolution. Our approach is based on rubric-induced self-consistency: independently sampled rubrics for the same query provide partial views of its latent evaluation requirements, and a comprehensive rubric should induce a response that generalizes across these complementary evaluation views. We implement this principle through reinforcement learning, combining a cross-rubric comprehensiveness signal with group-level and criterion-level rewards for rubric quality. We train GenRubric models at 4B, 8B, and 14B scales across multiple domains. Experiments on human-annotated rubric benchmarks show that self-evolution improves the agreement between evaluations induced by generated rubrics and those induced by expert-written rubrics. The improvements further generalize to held-out domains, demonstrating the potential of self-evolving rubric generation for scalable and query-specific LLM evaluation. Code and models are publicly available at https://github.com/foggpoy/GenRubric.

title: Interpreting and Steering for Safe and Correct Code Generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate source code containing vulnerabilities, yet little work studies the internal mechanisms that distinguish safe from vulnerable generation in them. In this work, we systematically perform a mechanistic interpretation of LLMs, aiming at both understanding how code safety-vs-vulnerability is represented or driven by components in an LM and turning the insights into actionable steering strategies to encourage safer code generation. To this end, we introduce CodeSec-Pairs, a dataset of 9,342 Python safe-and-vulnerable contrastive code pairs, sampled from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Utilizing the dataset, we explore approaches to localize layers and attention heads that relate to code safety, and further experiment with different steering strategies for inference-time vulnerability reduction. In particular, we propose DuoSteer, a double-steering approach that simultaneously applies safety and code-correctness steering to attention heads. In experiments over five vulnerability types, DuoSteer leads to an average of -26.9% vulnerability rate reduction and +7.5% functional correctness improvement, which outperforms not only other steering variants but also prompting and supervised fine-tuning baselines. The advantage also replicates on Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with another 2,500 contrastive pairs sampled from that model.

title: Small Language Models as Judges for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning extends RL beyond tasks with exact answers or rule-based verifiers by scoring responses against instance-specific criteria. However, this makes reward computation expensive: training requires repeated rubric judging, often with proprietary APIs or local generative LLM judges with 7B parameters or more. We study whether smaller language models can serve as efficient and reliable rubric-based judges. To make this question measurable, we construct PointRubric and RaR-Science-Static, two pointwise rubric-based evaluation datasets with instance-specific criteria and itemwise satisfaction labels. We compare three ways of extracting criterion-level judgments from small models: Generative verdicts, Yes/No Logprob margins, and Probe judges. Across both datasets, the Qwen3-1.7B Probe judge achieves the strongest criterion-level agreement among these methods, outperforming Generative and Logprob judges. Used as a GRPO reward model, it trains a policy from 0.232 to 0.643 on RaR-Science rubric score, compared with 0.594 for an 8B Generative judge baseline, while the baseline requires 10.7$\times$ more reward-judge time. Task and domain transfer experiments further suggest that Probe judges preserve criterion-level reward structure across settings.

title: Arkios: An Open Bilingual English-Nepali Language Model Trained From Scratch, with a Devanagari-Aware Tokenizer
abstract: We present Arkios, a 1.04B-parameter dense transformer pretrained from scratch on 150B tokens of bilingual English-Nepali text, using a custom single-file C/CUDA training stack and a Devanagari-aware byte-level BPE tokenizer built for this project. On ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge, Arkios exceeds three comparably sized open models (Pythia-1.4B, TinyLlama-1.1B, OLMo-1B) despite an order of magnitude fewer training tokens, likely aided by a match between our educational-web-text pretraining data and ARC's grade-school-science format rather than a general capability advantage. We report full evaluation results under standard protocols, including a correction to an earlier partial-sample estimate, and findings specific to evaluating small models in a low-resource language: the standard multiple-choice-letter prompt format used by common evaluation harnesses places this model at chance on Nepali reading comprehension, and simultaneously at chance on English in the same format, which would lead a naive benchmark run to conclude the model has no Nepali ability when in fact it does. Concretely, both languages score at chance in the letter-choice format (0.240 Nepali, 0.236 English, against a chance baseline of 0.250), while scoring the answer text directly reveals genuine, English-favoring comprehension (0.306 Nepali, 0.387 English). We describe a manifest-conditioned tool-use contract introduced during instruction tuning, where tool calls are permitted only when a tool manifest is declared in context and suppressed otherwise, and report where that contract holds and where it does not. We release both the base and instruction-tuned model weights under Apache-2.0. The training code and a small privately-sourced portion of the Nepali pretraining corpus are not released; everything needed to reproduce the reported numbers from the released weights is included here.

title: The Emergent Symbolic Structure of Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: Modern systems in artificial intelligence (AI) somehow excel in domains for which they seem poorly suited. Intelligence has traditionally been modeled as operating over structured combinations of symbols, such as logical formulas. However, the strongest modern AI systems are based on neural networks, which instead represent information in continuous vectors. Vectors seem inadequate for capturing the structure of language, logic, and other cognitive domains, yet neural networks achieve impressive performance in these areas. How do they do it? In this work, we propose a potential answer: Despite appearances, perhaps the internal representations of neural networks implicitly realize symbolic structure. In support of this hypothesis, we show that the vector representations of a variety of neural networks can be closely approximated with symbolic structures: we can replace the network's entire representation-generating process with a closed-form equation instantiating a symbolic structure, and the network's behavior remains largely unchanged. This finding holds for both small-scale neural networks trained to manipulate lists as well as large language models (LLMs) operating in four domains that are central in symbolic traditions: arithmetic, logic, computer code, and language. Further, our symbolic approximation allows us to modify an LLM's behavior in targeted ways via precise interventions on its internal representations, showing that the LLM's behavior is reliant on the symbolic structures we have identified. This work provides a potential way to reconcile longstanding symbolic conceptions of intelligence with the vector-based nature of modern AI.

title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Sampled-token on-policy distillation (OPD) efficiently transfers capabilities from teacher to student using student-generated tokens, requiring teacher probabilities only for sampled tokens. Yet it frequently suffers from diversity distillation failure: the student's pass@1 improves while its pass@$k$ plateaus, failing to inherit the teacher's diversity. To explain this, we introduce First-Order Local Entropy Influence, a signed first-order proxy that decouples each update's entropy effect into the teacher--student log-probability gap and the student's local probability structure, and empirically links entropy contraction to negative-influence positions. Motivated by this, we propose Influence-Directed Adaptive On-Policy Distillation (IDA-OPD): rather than relying on costly full-vocabulary Forward-KL objectives, it preserves entropy-expanding updates while replacing entropy-contracting ones with divergence-adaptive advantage shrinkage, using only the teacher's sampled-token log-probability. Experiments on reasoning-oriented distillation show IDA-OPD consistently improves pass@$k$, inheriting the teacher's diversity through distillation, matches the strongest teacher-informed methods at strictly lower cost, and broadly maintains vanilla OPD's pass@1, all without full-vocabulary teacher information.

title: Not Safe for All: Auditing the Dialect Penalty in Text-to-Image Safety Pipelines
abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) safety guardrails fail to generalize equitably to non-standard dialects. Evaluating 23,080 paired prompts across five English dialects, we formalize this failure as the dialect penalty, where filters trigger based on linguistic surface features rather than semantic intent. Text-level filters fail in opposing directions: NSFW-T over-flags benign dialect prompts and LatentGuard over-flags toxic ones (bias gaps up to +28.29 pp), while the OpenAI Moderation API under-detects them. A controlled typo ablation confirms this penalty originates from flagging dialectal features, not generic out-of-distribution sensitivity. The pixel-level generator is largely dialect-agnostic; the penalty enters at text processing and cascades unevenly to post-hoc guardrails. We show this bias tracks training data imbalance and is mitigable via group-balanced retraining, with an ablation attributing the gain to balanced exposure rather than to the worst-group objective of GroupDRO (group distributionally robust optimization). Current pipelines systematically fail dialect speakers, an equity failure masked by mean accuracy benchmarks. Our official code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/minguinho26/dialect-penalty-t2i. Content Warning: This paper contains offensive, toxic, or disturbing text prompts and generated images.
